responsibility: This larger tutorial example implements a tiny stack-based virtual machine in C together with a libgccjit-based compiler for its bytecode-like operations. It parses .toy scripts into toyvm_function and toyvm_op structures, interprets them directly for reference behavior, then translates each opcode into libgccjit blocks, locals, calls, comparisons, and jumps to produce native code and verify that compiled execution matches the interpreter. Its role is to demonstrate nontrivial JIT lowering from an interpreter IR to libgccjit IR.
same_name_distinction: Unlike gcc/jit/docs/examples/tut04-toyvm/toyvm.cc, this same-stem toy VM implementation is the C version: it uses C structs and functions for the interpreter/compiler and lowers bytecode through the raw libgccjit C API.
